subject: Dedicated capacity start schedule + throughput guarantees (SkywardAI)
messages:
From: Mira Solis <mira.solis@skywardai.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@skywardai.com
Date: 2027-02-20T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Dedicated capacity start window + throughput guarantees

Hi Jordan,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the team liked Redwood's latency profile. Procurement asked me to follow up on two items before we take the commercial draft to legal:

1) Term options: they want a clear comparison between 12/24/36-month reserved commit pricing and the incremental discounts you can offer if we pick 24 vs 36 months.
2) Start window & ramp: our preferred start is April 1. We need to understand realistic GPU pool sizing (NVIDIA A10 vs A100-equivalent), a suggested ramp schedule (weeks to reach committed throughput), and what happens if we miss the April 1 activation (credits? delayed billing?).

I've attached the latest SOW for context. Can you share a short table with: committed vCPU/GPU, target tokens/s, SLO (p95 latency), and the discount applied at each term? Procurement will want to see throughput guarantees tied to SLA credits.

Mira
Mira Solis
Head of Platform Ops, SkywardAI

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Mira Solis <mira.solis@skywardai.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, procurement@skywardai.com
Date: 2027-02-20T11:34:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity start window + throughput guarantees

Mira — thanks for the clear asks and the SOW. Attached is a concise pricing/options file (Dedicated_Pricing_Options.xlsx) but below is the short version so procurement has something to review immediately.

High-level options (monthly effective $/GPU-hour, committed pool):
- 12-month: baseline pricing, no ramp credits, standard support.  (No term discount)
- 24-month: 8% term discount on baseline + 10% onboarding credit if start by 2027-04-15
- 36-month: 13% term discount + 15% onboarding credit and priority capacity scheduling

GPU sizing suggestion (for expected workload from SOW):
- Option A (balanced): 8 x A10-equivalent nodes — expected steady throughput ~55k tokens/s (batched) — p95 inference latency target ~220ms
- Option B (throughput-first): 12 x A10/A100-mix — expected steady throughput ~95k tokens/s — p95 ~180ms

Ramp schedule (typical):
- Week 0: capacity reserved, staging cluster provisioned
- Week 1–2: model load + prefix cache warmup, 30–50% of committed throughput
- Week 3–4: steady state to committed throughput

Missed activation policy (if start delayed beyond agreed start date):
- If start <= 30 days late: deferred billing with pro-rated onboarding credit preserved
- If start 31–90 days late: onboarding credit reduced by 50%
- If start >90 days: option to re-negotiate term or roll to a later tier (no automatic penalty but pricing reset)

Throughput guarantees & SLA credits:
- SLA measured on 95th-percentile per-route latency and token throughput availability. If we fail throughput guarantee for > 3 days in a 30-day window, customer receives service credits up to 10% of monthly committed fee (stacked per additional breach up to 25%).

I've CC'd Karthik and Laura to pull margin/discount flexibility and to advise on operational protections. Happy to hop on a 30-min call this week to walk procurement through the spreadsheet.

—Jordan
Jordan Blake
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Mira Solis <mira.solis@skywardai.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, procurement@skywardai.com
Date: 2027-02-21T08:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity start window + throughput guarantees

Mira — quick follow from commercial: we can flex the 24-month term to 10% discount (was 8%) if Skyward commits to a 6-month accelerate clause: if you accelerate consumption >120% of committed tokens for two consecutive months, we guarantee an additional 5% rebate on that overage (capped at 50% of month spend) — this helps us protect scheduling while giving Skyward a runway for growth.

Also: for the April 1 start the onboarding credit (10% at 24m) will be applied to the first two invoices as a one-line credit; if Skyward needs an April 15 grace, we can still honor full credit.

I'll let legal weigh in on exact contract language, but commercially we can push to 10% on 24m with the accelerate clause.

Karthik
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Mira Solis <mira.solis@skywardai.com>
Cc: procurement@skywardai.com
Date: 2027-02-22T10:42:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity start window + throughput guarantees

Adding a small ops protection request from our side: if we agree to a hard April 1 start with onboarding credits tied to that date, please add a one-time "start-delay hold" — a 30-day courtesy window where billing doesn't start and we keep the credit intact if Skyward provides a written delay notice. Beyond 30 days we follow Jordan's outlined reductions. This preserves commercial predictability for both sides.

Also, recommend we lock the p95 SLO definition into the SOW windows (model routes defined) rather than a generic "p95" — that keeps measurement precise and avoids disputes in month 1.

Laura Bennett
Director, Customer Success, Redwood Inference

From: Mira Solis <mira.solis@skywardai.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@skywardai.com
Date: 2027-02-24T14:10:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity start window + throughput guarantees

Thanks — that all looks reasonable. A few clarifications from procurement: 

- Skyward prefers the 24-month option if you can move to 10% term discount and preserve the 10% onboarding credit with an April 15 soft start allowance.
- We accept the accelerate clause parameters but propose the rebate cap be 75% of month spend (instead of 50%).
- For GPU sizing: we want the balanced Option A to start and a documented pathway to bump to Option B within 45 days if traffic growth requires it. Please add a pricing delta for the scale-up event (per-GPU hourly adder).

We can proceed to legal once the pricing spreadsheet includes the revised 24m discount, the revised rebate cap, and the scale-up adder. Also please confirm whether DocuSign routing will include our procurement contact (procurement@skywardai.com).

Mira

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Mira Solis <mira.solis@skywardai.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-02-25T15:04:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity start window + throughput guarantees

Mira — great, thanks for the quick alignment. Action items and next steps: 

1) I'll update Dedicated_Pricing_Options.xlsx to reflect: 24m = 10% term discount; accelerate rebate cap = 75%; scale-up adder = +$12/GPU-hour for additional nodes beyond the committed pool (pro-rated hourly).
2) We'll insert a 30-day start-delay hold clause into the SOW and lock the p95 routes into the SOW appendix.
3) I'll route the DocuSign envelope to procurement@skywardai.com and Mira (primary). Expect the envelope tomorrow.
4) Proposed kickoff: 2027-04-01 staging + smoke tests; production ramp Week 3 after start. If you need the April 15 soft-start we will adjust the onboarding credit logic as discussed.

Attachments uploaded to the deal record: Skyward_SOW_v2.pdf, Dedicated_Pricing_Options.xlsx

If that all sounds good I'll kick the DocuSign and we can schedule a 30-minute runbook sync next week.

—Jordan
Jordan Blake
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
